images.caption: Figure 1:ForcingBooster accelerates interactive video generation and world model by adaptively allocating different denoising steps to different patches. Heatmap overlays visualize router allocations from matching conditional samples:static backgrounds need fewer updates than moving objects, new regions or detailed textures.

Figure 2:Adaptive patch-wise inference and on-policy router training.(a) The router selects patches to continue denoising; stopped predictions provide reusable KV context. (b) A no-gradient rollout records exits for replay. Reconstruction and computational costs train the router through its stopping probabilities.

Figure 3:Denoising steps required by different patches.Left: fixed-step generation results with enlarged local details. Right: patch-wise first-hit step distribution at35​dB35\,\mathrm{dB}PSNR relative to the four-step reference in a separate controlled experiment.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison.The rows show the results from four-step baseline to one-step sampling, and ForcingBooster. One-step and Two-step sampling exhibits a decline in quality and visible artifacts. Red boxes indicate visual artifacts.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison across additional models.ForcingBooster produces visual results comparable to the four-step baseline, while uniform one-step sampling often exhibits a decline in quality and visible artifacts. Red boxes indicate visual artifacts.
Figure 6:Qualitative comparison of computation allocation.Columns show frames at matching time points under the same generation conditions. Red boxes indicate visual artifacts.
